title: Ibn Abbas
hook: the young cousin, prayed for to understand the religion, later the great interpreter (Bukhari)

segments.voice: Yesterday: ijtihad, and Mu'adh ibn Jabal's three steps for judging. Your line was book, sunnah, reason.

A jug of water has been set out. Nobody asked for it. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, comes to wash, finds it waiting, and asks: who put this here? Someone tells him: Abdullah, the son of your uncle Abbas. A boy, who had noticed what would be needed and quietly set it out. And instead of a thank you, the Prophet says a short prayer for him, one line the boy will carry for the rest of his life. Today: Ibn Abbas.
screen: `A JUG OF WATER, SET OUT.` → `WHO PUT THIS HERE?` → `A ONE-LINE PRAYER FOR A BOY.`

segments.voice: Sahih al-Bukhari records the prayer: O God, give him understanding of the religion. In Arabic, the prayer asks that he be given fiqh in the religion, the word later used for the study of Islamic law. In another report in Bukhari, Ibn Abbas says the Prophet held him close and prayed: O God, teach him the book. Did it show? Bukhari keeps a scene that answers. Years later, Umar, now leading the community, used to bring young Ibn Abbas into his council with the older men who had fought at Badr. Some of them objected: why does he sit with us, when we have sons his age? So one day Umar asked the whole group about the surah that begins: when the help of God comes, and the victory. Some said it tells us to praise God and seek His forgiveness when victory comes. Others said nothing. Then Umar turned to Ibn Abbas. Is that what you say too? No, he said. It was the sign of the Prophet's own approaching death, given to him by God: when the victory comes, your work is done; praise your Lord and ask forgiveness. Umar answered: I know nothing of it except what you have said. The older men gave the plain meaning, and it was true. The young man saw what the surah was pointing to. Tradition remembers Ibn Abbas as an interpreter of the Qur'an. It started with a jug of water and a one-line prayer. Understanding, prayed for.
screen: `O GOD, GIVE HIM UNDERSTANDING.` · `O GOD, TEACH HIM THE BOOK.` · `UMAR'S QUESTION ABOUT SURAH 110.` · `THE YOUNG MAN UNDERSTOOD.` · then, large: `UNDERSTANDING PRAYED FOR.`

segments.voice: Take the first line of surah one hundred ten, when the help of God comes, and the victory, and say it once, slowly. Then ask Ibn Abbas's kind of question, not only what it says but what it is doing, who it speaks to, what moment it is for, and sit with it without hurrying. If you pray, you can ask, as the Prophet asked for him, for understanding.

Ibn Abbas. Abdullah, son of the Prophet's uncle Abbas, prayed for as a boy to understand the religion and the book, and remembered as an interpreter of the Qur'an. Today's word, and the last of the early believers.
Your line: understanding prayed for. Tomorrow the path turns to the later companions and their stories. See you there.

howItsDone: Muslims remember Abdullah ibn Abbas as a companion known for explaining the Qur'an, and retell the hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari where the Prophet prayed for him to be given understanding of the religion.

pray for him: O God, give him understanding of the religion.

original.note: Arabic: 'understanding'; the word in the prayer 'give him understanding of the religion', and later the name for Islamic law.

chat.says: What did the Prophet pray for when Ibn Abbas set out the water?
options: O God, give him understanding of the religion. Another report: teach him the book.
That God grant him wealth and a long life, as thanks for his kindness.
That God make him a leader of armies, like the older men at Badr.
chat.meaning: In Bukhari the Prophet prayed: O God, give him understanding of the religion; in another report, O God, teach him the book.

fiqh.meaning: understanding; later the name for the study of Islamic law

Badr.meaning: a battle whose veterans were honored elders

Umar.meaning: the companion then leading the community

Abbas.meaning: the Prophet's uncle, father of Ibn Abbas

notes: Audit: 'The older men had read the words; the young man had understood' belittled the Badr companions, whose reading is also accepted; now says their plain meaning was true and Ibn Abbas saw what the surah pointed to.
Last day of the part 'Early believers (823–836)'; the carry points to the next part, later companions.
Hadith numbers cited from memory; confirm Bukhari 143, 75 and 4970.
Bukhari 143 has 'faqqihhu fid-din'; the original note links it to the root of fiqh. Confirm.
Surah 110 verses paraphrased, not quoted from Pickthall.
In Bukhari 4970 the objecting men are not named individually ('some of them' / Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf in some versions); kept general.
